summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and breast cancer presented with acute nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and fever following consumption of spoiled food. Initially suspected to have viral gastroenteritis, she was found to have pyelonephritis caused by Enterobacter cloacae. She also developed acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration and hypophosphatemia. She was treated with intravenous fluids, antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin. Her cyclosporine dose was reduced due to elevated levels, and she was started on phosphorus supplementation. Her symptoms resolved, kidney function normalized, and she was discharged home with a plan for close nephrology follow-up and completion of antibiotics.
problems: Acute pyelonephritis without lesion of renal medullary necrosis
Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified
